findings.title: IDOR via Base64-Encoded User ID Cookie - Flag Extracted
findings.description:
The application stores the authenticated user's company ID in a cookie named 'access_token' as a Bearer token where the token value is simply the user ID base64-encoded (e.g., MQ== = 1, Mg== = 2). An attacker can modify this cookie to access any other company's data without authorization.

Exploit steps:
1. Login as demo/demo — receives cookie: access_token="Bearer MQ==" (base64(1))
2. Change cookie to access_token="Bearer Mg==" (base64(2)) to impersonate company 2
3. Access /company/2/jobs — returns company 2's confidential job listings including the flag

diagrams.title: CTF App Architecture - IDOR Vulnerability
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  Browser["Browser / Attacker"] --> Login["/token POST - Login"]
  Login --> Cookie["Set-Cookie: access_token=Bearer base64(userID)"]
  Cookie --> Jobs["/company/{id}/jobs - View Jobs"]
  Cookie --> Profile["/edit_profile/{id} - Edit Profile"]
  Jobs --> IDOR["IDOR: Change cookie base64(1) to base64(2)"]
  IDOR --> FlagData["Company 2 Jobs - Contains FLAG"]
  FlagData --> Flag["flag{0d8ca439-1cc2-4de9-a83f-08182aede041}"]
